decision: FAIL: Mirror misses 20% byte gate and matches generic free factorization; independent experts need free factors
facts: Aligned: Mirror and generic factorization both held-out output NRMSE ~2.98e-4; Mirror 1,552 B vs generic 1,745 B (11% smaller, below 20% gate).
Flat Tucker per-combination coefficients have held-out NRMSE 1.0 because unseen coefficients are zero; payload 5,305 B.
Independent expert factors: generic free factorization NRMSE ~2.86e-4; Mirror NRMSE ~1.073.
interpretation: Factorizing layer×expert Tucker coefficients generalizes held-out combinations well, but the generic free A×B factorization matches Mirror and exceeds its registered storage gate. Mirror is unnecessary for this factorized family; independent expert bases remain private.
hypothesis: Rejected for Mirror-specific value; generic factorization accounts for held-out combination gains.
counter_hypothesis: Larger coefficient banks or varying factor ranks could change the relative code size; outside this fixed K=8 protocol.
limitations: Coefficient values observed directly for training pairs; no network optimization
No learned router or real Transformer
Fixed balanced deterministic basis and factorization
